\chapter{Games and Films}
\label{ch:ml-leisure}
\hlchaptermodality{98}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can name a game, say that I play, and name a film.}

From cold: the three leisure words, and what actually decides the letter that slides in before aaNu.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[kaḷi]{\ml{കളി} (kaḷi) — a game}

\label{lesson:ML-C98-kali}



\begin{quote}
Say \emph{this is beautiful} — the word and the ending together.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\textbf{\ml{കളി}} — \emph{kaḷi} — \textbf{a game}, and also \textbf{play} itself.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ml{ഇത്} \ml{കളിയാണ്}.} — \emph{itŭ kaḷiyāṇŭ} — \textquotedblleft{}This is a game.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{You built that ending without being told.} \textbf{\ml{കളി}} ends in the same vowel \textbf{\ml{ഭംഗി}} does, so the same \textbf{\ml{യ}} slides in before \textbf{\ml{ആണ്}}:

\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{word} & \textbf{joined to \textbf{\ml{ആണ്}}} \\
\midrule
\textbf{\ml{ഭംഗി}} & \textbf{\ml{ഭംഗിയാണ്}} (\emph{bhaṁgiyāṇŭ}) \\
\textbf{\ml{കളി}} & \textbf{\ml{കളിയാണ്}} (\emph{kaḷiyāṇŭ}) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

\textbf{You have seen this done before, and not only last chapter.} \textbf{\ml{കുട്ടി}} has been taking the same \textbf{\ml{യ}} since \textbf{\ml{ഇത്} \ml{എന്റെ} \ml{കുട്ടിയാണ്}}, and for the same reason: the word ends in a vowel, \textbf{\ml{ആണ്}} begins with one, and something has to stand between them.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
\textbf{This is the book's first word for play.}

You could already say that you read, that you eat, that you work, that you go. Every one of those has a point outside itself. \textbf{\ml{കളി}} names the kind of doing that is its own point — and until this lesson the book had given you no word for it.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{kaḷi}
  \item \emph{itŭ kaḷiyāṇŭ}
  \item \emph{bhaṁgiyāṇŭ}, then \emph{kaḷiyāṇŭ}, and hear the part they share
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What is \emph{a game}? (\textbf{\ml{കളി}}.) \textbf{\ml{കളി}} ends in \textbf{\ml{ഇ}} — which letter slides in before \textbf{\ml{ആണ്}}? (\textbf{\ml{യ}} — the same one \textbf{\ml{ഭംഗി}} and \textbf{\ml{കുട്ടി}} take.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[kaḷikkuka]{\ml{കളിക്കുക} (kaḷikkuka) — to play}

\label{lesson:ML-C98-kalikkuka}



\begin{quote}
Say \emph{a game}. Then say \emph{to read}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\textbf{\ml{കളിക്കുക}} — \emph{kaḷikkuka} — \textbf{to play.}

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ml{ഞാൻ} \ml{കളിക്കുന്നു}.} — \emph{ñān kaḷikkunnu} — \textquotedblleft{}I play.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{The noun is sitting inside the verb.} \textbf{\ml{കളി}} is the game; \textbf{\ml{കളിക്കുക}} is doing it.

And the shape is one you have had for a long time. Put it beside the reading verb:

\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{} & \textbf{} \\
\midrule
\textbf{\ml{വായിക്കുക}} $\to$ \textbf{\ml{വായിക്കുന്നു}} & reads \\
\textbf{\ml{കളിക്കുക}} $\to$ \textbf{\ml{കളിക്കുന്നു}} & plays \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

\textbf{Verb after verb in this book already ends in -\ml{ിക്കുക}} — \textbf{\ml{സംസാരിക്കുക}}, \textbf{\ml{വായിക്കുക}}, \textbf{\ml{ചോദിക്കുക}}, \textbf{\ml{കുടിക്കുക}} — so this one arrives asking nothing new of you. The only new part is the two syllables at the front.
\end{cousinweb}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaḷikkuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ñān kaḷikkunnu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vāyikkunnu}, then \emph{kaḷikkunnu}
  \item \emph{Look:} at \textbf{\ml{കളി}} inside \textbf{\ml{കളിക്കുക}}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What is \emph{to play}? (\textbf{\ml{കളിക്കുക}}.) What word can you see inside it? (\textbf{\ml{കളി}}.) Did its ending need learning? (\textbf{No} — the reading verb already had it.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[sinima]{\ml{സിനിമ} (sinima) — a film}

\label{lesson:ML-C98-sinima}



\begin{quote}
Say \emph{a game}. Then say the borrowed word for a place that serves food.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\textbf{\ml{സിനിമ}} — \emph{sinima} — \textbf{a film}, and \textbf{the cinema} as well.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ml{ഇത്} \ml{നല്ല} \ml{സിനിമയാണ്}.} — \emph{itŭ nalla sinimayāṇŭ} — \textquotedblleft{}This is a good film.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{A borrowed word again}, like the eating-place word — and this one kept far more of what it came with than that one did.

Its last letter is \textbf{\ml{മ}}, and a consonant in this script carries an \emph{a} of its own: \textbf{\ml{മ}} is \emph{ma}. So \textbf{\ml{സിനിമ}} ends in a full vowel, \textbf{\ml{ആണ്}} opens with one, and — as with \textbf{\ml{കളി}} — something has to stand between the two.

Here that something is \textbf{\ml{യ}} once more: \textbf{\ml{സിനിമയാണ്}}.

\textbf{Do not read that as \emph{a vowel brings \ml{യ}}.} Which letter slides in is settled by \emph{which} vowel the word ends in, and you already have one that goes the other way:

\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{ends in} & \textbf{word} & \textbf{joined to \textbf{\ml{ആണ്}}} \\
\midrule
\textbf{\ml{ഇ}} & \textbf{\ml{ഭംഗി}} & \textbf{\ml{ഭംഗിയാണ്}} (\emph{bhaṁgiyāṇŭ}) \\
\textbf{\ml{ഇ}} & \textbf{\ml{കളി}} & \textbf{\ml{കളിയാണ്}} (\emph{kaḷiyāṇŭ}) \\
\textbf{\ml{അ}} & \textbf{\ml{സിനിമ}} & \textbf{\ml{സിനിമയാണ്}} (\emph{sinimayāṇŭ}) \\
\textbf{\ml{ഉ}} & \textbf{\ml{പശു}} & \textbf{\ml{പശുവാണ്}} (\emph{paśuvāṇŭ}) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

\textbf{The cow is the row to look at.} \textbf{\ml{ഇ}} and \textbf{\ml{അ}} both take \textbf{\ml{യ}}; a full \textbf{\ml{ഉ}} takes \textbf{\ml{വ}}. The gap gets filled either way — the vowel at the end says with what.

\textbf{The faint half-u is not one of these vowels.} Look back at the sentence above: \textbf{\ml{ഇത്}} stands right beside \textbf{\ml{സിനിമയാണ്}}, and nothing slides into \textbf{\ml{ഇത്}} at all. That breathed \textbf{-ŭ} at the end of a word is not a full vowel — it simply steps out of the way. \textbf{\ml{എന്ത്}} has been doing it since your very first question: \textbf{\ml{എന്ത്}} + \textbf{\ml{ആണ്}} is \textbf{\ml{എന്താണ്}}, \emph{entāṇŭ}, with nothing added and one sound quietly given up.
\end{cousinweb}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{sinima}
  \item \emph{itŭ nalla sinimayāṇŭ}
  \item the four joined forms in the table, one after another
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What is \emph{a film}? (\textbf{\ml{സിനിമ}}.) \textbf{\ml{സിനിമ}} ends in \textbf{\ml{അ}} — what slides in before \textbf{\ml{ആണ്}}? (\textbf{\ml{യ}} — \textbf{\ml{സിനിമയാണ്}}.) And \textbf{\ml{പശു}}, which ends in \textbf{\ml{ഉ}}? (\textbf{\ml{വ}} — \textbf{\ml{പശുവാണ്}}, \emph{paśuvāṇŭ}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[kaḷiyuṁ sinimayuṁ enna ōrmma]{(a game, playing, a film) — from cold}

\label{lesson:ML-R98-leisure-recall}



\begin{quote}
Close the lessons before this one. Say \emph{a game}, then \emph{to play}, then \emph{a film}.
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: the vowel at the end chooses}]
\textbf{\ml{ആണ്}} opens with a vowel. A word that ends in a \textbf{full} vowel cannot sit straight against it, so a letter comes in between. \textbf{Which letter is not free} — the word's own last vowel settles it:

\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{ends in} & \textbf{word} & \textbf{joined to \textbf{\ml{ആണ്}}} \\
\midrule
\textbf{\ml{ഇ}} & \textbf{\ml{ഭംഗി}} & \textbf{\ml{ഭംഗിയാണ്}} (\emph{bhaṁgiyāṇŭ}) \\
\textbf{\ml{ഇ}} & \textbf{\ml{കളി}} & \textbf{\ml{കളിയാണ്}} (\emph{kaḷiyāṇŭ}) \\
\textbf{\ml{അ}} & \textbf{\ml{സിനിമ}} & \textbf{\ml{സിനിമയാണ്}} (\emph{sinimayāṇŭ}) \\
\textbf{\ml{ഉ}} & \textbf{\ml{പശു}} & \textbf{\ml{പശുവാണ്}} (\emph{paśuvāṇŭ}) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

\textbf{Three rows out of four take \ml{യ}, and that is exactly why the fourth is worth holding on to.} If you carry away \emph{vowels take \ml{യ}}, the cow will catch you out. What you want is \emph{the last vowel decides} — and \textbf{\ml{ഇ}} and \textbf{\ml{അ}} happen to decide the same way, while \textbf{\ml{ഉ}} does not.

\textbf{And the breathed half-u at the end of a word is not in this table at all.} \textbf{\ml{എന്ത്}} + \textbf{\ml{ആണ്}} is \textbf{\ml{എന്താണ്}} — \emph{entāṇŭ} — with nothing slid in and that faint \textbf{-ŭ} given up instead. \textbf{\ml{ഇത്}} does the same. Those are not words ending in a full vowel, so the question the table answers never arises for them.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
\textbf{\ml{കളി}} is the game. \textbf{\ml{കളിക്കുക}} is doing it — the noun still visible inside the verb, wearing an ending you had long before this chapter:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ml{ഞാൻ} \ml{വായിക്കുന്നു}.} — I read.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ml{ഞാൻ} \ml{കളിക്കുന്നു}.} — I play.
\end{quote}

Two lines built the same way, and only one of them was ever taught to you as a pattern. The other you assembled.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{kaḷi}, \emph{kaḷikkuka}, \emph{sinima}
  \item \emph{itŭ kaḷiyāṇŭ}, then \emph{itŭ nalla sinimayāṇŭ}
  \item \emph{ñān kaḷikkunnu}
  \item which of the four table rows takes \textbf{\ml{വ}}, and what it ends in
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A game, to play, a film? (\textbf{\ml{കളി}, \ml{കളിക്കുക}, \ml{സിനിമ}}.) What decides the letter that slides in before \textbf{\ml{ആണ്}}? (\textbf{The full vowel the word ends in}.) Which of these four ends in \textbf{\ml{ഉ}}? (\textbf{\ml{പശു}} — \textbf{\ml{പശുവാണ്}}, \emph{paśuvāṇŭ}.) And what does \textbf{\ml{എന്ത്}} do instead? (\textbf{Nothing slides in} — \textbf{\ml{എന്താണ്}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
